brief.title: Usage-based Billing & Invoicing Platform
business_goals: Transition from flat-rate to usage-based pricing per API call.
Scale billing operations beyond 400 customers, eliminating manual spreadsheet reconciliation.
Provide customers with real-time visibility into their API usage, updated within a few minutes.
Accurately calculate tiered charges to ensure correct revenue recognition.
Implement usage alerts for customers when they hit 80% of any self-set spending cap.
Generate and send invoices within 24 hours of the billing period closing.
Automate dunning and failed-payment retry logic (retry a failed card three times over a week).
Handle high volume of metering events (40 million API calls/month per customer) without dropping events to prevent billing disputes.
Retain seven years of invoice and usage data for tax and audit purposes.
Reduce inter-departmental 'Slack fire drills' caused by billing discrepancies.

stakeholders.name: Chris Nakamura
concerns: Customers needing real-time visibility into their usage.
Customers receiving usage alerts (e.g., 80% of spending cap).
Managing scope, specifically multi-currency billing being out of scope for this phase.

stakeholders.name: Omar Haddad
concerns: Billing system consuming metering events from existing Kafka topic (fed by Kong API gateway).
Metering pipeline handling high volume (40 million API calls/month per customer) without dropping events.
Reducing manual reconciliation and 'Slack fire drills' caused by billing discrepancies.

stakeholders.name: Grace Lindqvist
concerns: Invoices being sent through Stripe as the existing payment processor.
Automatic dunning and failed-payment retry logic.

constraints: Must consume usage events from an existing Kafka topic.
Must use Stripe as the existing payment processor for invoicing.
Metering pipeline must handle 40 million API calls/month per customer without dropping events.
Seven years of invoice and usage data must be retained for tax and audit purposes.
System must be live before July 1st (fiscal year start).
Project budget is capped at $400,000 (including Kafka and Stripe integration work).

epics.title: Usage Data Ingestion & Processing
epics.goal: To reliably capture and process all customer API usage data, eliminating manual reconciliation.

epics.title: Usage-based Charge Calculation
epics.goal: To accurately calculate customer charges based on their API usage and contracted rates, including tiered pricing.

epics.title: Customer Usage Visibility & Alerts
epics.goal: To provide customers with timely visibility into their API usage and notify them of spending cap thresholds.

epics.title: Invoice Generation & Payment Management
epics.goal: To automate the generation, delivery, and payment processing of customer invoices, including handling failed payments.

epics.title: Data Retention & Audit Readiness
epics.goal: To securely store all necessary billing and usage data for seven years to meet tax and audit requirements.

stories.title: Ingest Metering Events
stories.i_want: to consume metering events from Kafka
stories.so_that: all customer API usage is captured for billing

acceptance_criteria.given: A Kafka topic contains new API metering events
acceptance_criteria.when: The billing system starts consuming events
acceptance_criteria.then: A monitoring dashboard shows the count of ingested events matching the count of events published to the Kafka topic

acceptance_criteria.given: The Kafka topic receives 40 million API calls per month for a single customer
acceptance_criteria.when: The billing system processes these events
acceptance_criteria.then: A monitoring dashboard shows zero dropped events and the count of processed events matches the count of consumed events

stories.title: Process Raw Usage Data
stories.i_want: usage data to be automatically aggregated and stored
stories.so_that: manual spreadsheet reconciliation is eliminated and billing discrepancies are reduced

acceptance_criteria.given: Raw metering events have been ingested for a customer
acceptance_criteria.when: The system processes the raw events
acceptance_criteria.then: Aggregated usage data is stored per customer per billing period

acceptance_criteria.given: Duplicate metering events are ingested
acceptance_criteria.when: The system processes the events
acceptance_criteria.then: Only unique usage events are counted in the aggregated data

stories.title: Calculate Base Usage Charges
stories.i_want: to calculate charges based on a contracted rate per thousand API calls
stories.so_that: accurate usage-based pricing is applied to customer accounts

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer has consumed 1,500 API calls and has a contracted rate of $10 per 1,000 calls
acceptance_criteria.when: The system calculates the base charges
acceptance_criteria.then: The calculated charge is $15.00

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer has consumed 0 API calls
acceptance_criteria.when: The system calculates the base charges
acceptance_criteria.then: The calculated charge is $0.00

stories.title: Calculate Tiered Usage Charges
stories.so_that: charges are calculated correctly according to customer contracts

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer has a tiered contract: $10/1000 for 0-10,000 calls, $8/1000 for 10,001-50,000 calls. They consumed 15,000 calls.
acceptance_criteria.when: The system calculates the tiered charges
acceptance_criteria.then: The calculated charge is $140.00

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer has a tiered contract and consumed calls only within the first tier
acceptance_criteria.when: The system calculates the tiered charges
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the first tier rate is applied to the total calls

stories.title: Display Current Billing Period Usage
stories.i_want: to see my API calls consumed so far this billing period
stories.so_that: I have real-time visibility into my usage

acceptance_criteria.given: I am logged into the customer portal
acceptance_criteria.when: I navigate to the "Usage" section
acceptance_criteria.then: My total API calls consumed for the current billing period are displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: New API calls are made by my account
acceptance_criteria.when: I refresh the "Usage" section after 3 minutes
acceptance_criteria.then: The displayed API call count is updated to reflect the new usage

stories.title: Notify Customer of Usage Alerts
stories.i_want: to be notified when I hit 80% of my self-set spending cap
stories.so_that: I can manage my spending and avoid unexpected charges

acceptance_criteria.given: My self-set spending cap is $100 and my current usage charges reach $80
acceptance_criteria.when: The system processes my usage
acceptance_criteria.then: An email alert is sent to my registered email address

acceptance_criteria.given: My self-set spending cap is $100 and my current usage charges are $79
acceptance_criteria.when: The system processes my usage
acceptance_criteria.then: No email alert is sent

stories.title: Generate and Send Invoices
stories.i_want: to generate and send invoices through Stripe
stories.so_that: customers receive their bills promptly and payments can be processed

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer's billing period has closed
acceptance_criteria.when: The automated invoice generation process runs
acceptance_criteria.then: An invoice is generated with correct usage charges and sent to Stripe within 24 hours

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer has no usage for the billing period
acceptance_criteria.when: The automated invoice generation process runs
acceptance_criteria.then: A zero-balance invoice is generated and sent to Stripe

stories.title: Automate Failed Payment Retries
stories.i_want: the system to automatically retry failed card payments
stories.so_that: we recover revenue without manual intervention

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer's payment for an invoice fails
acceptance_criteria.when: The system detects the failed payment
acceptance_criteria.then: The system schedules the first retry attempt for the failed card within 24 hours of the initial failure

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer's payment fails on the third retry attempt
acceptance_criteria.when: The system processes the final failed attempt
acceptance_criteria.then: The system marks the invoice as uncollectible and sends a notification to the billing operations team

stories.title: Automate Dunning Process
stories.i_want: the system to automate dunning logic for overdue invoices
stories.so_that: we can recover outstanding payments efficiently

acceptance_criteria.given: An invoice is overdue after all payment retries have failed
acceptance_criteria.when: The system identifies the overdue invoice
acceptance_criteria.then: The system sends an overdue notice email to the customer's registered email address

acceptance_criteria.given: A customer pays an overdue invoice during the dunning process
acceptance_criteria.when: The system receives payment confirmation
acceptance_criteria.then: The dunning process for that invoice is halted

stories.title: Retain Invoice Data for Audit
stories.i_want: invoice data to be retained for seven years
stories.so_that: we can meet tax and audit compliance requirements

acceptance_criteria.given: An invoice is generated and stored
acceptance_criteria.when: Seven years pass from the invoice date
acceptance_criteria.then: The invoice data is queryable and retrievable in the system for audit purposes

acceptance_criteria.given: An auditor requests invoice data from five years ago
acceptance_criteria.when: The finance department queries the system
acceptance_criteria.then: The system displays the requested invoice data

stories.title: Retain Usage Data for Audit
stories.i_want: usage data to be retained for seven years
stories.so_that: we can meet tax and audit compliance requirements

acceptance_criteria.given: Aggregated usage data is stored for a billing period
acceptance_criteria.when: Seven years pass from the end of the billing period
acceptance_criteria.then: The usage data is queryable and retrievable in the system for audit purposes

acceptance_criteria.given: An auditor requests detailed usage data from three years ago
acceptance_criteria.when: The finance department queries the system
acceptance_criteria.then: The system displays the requested usage data

issues: AC1: 'Aggregated usage data is stored per customer per billing period' is vague. What specific data points are aggregated (e.g., total calls, unique users) and over what time period (e.g., daily, hourly)?
AC2: 'Only unique usage events are counted' is vague. What constitutes a 'unique usage event'? Is it based on a specific event ID, or a combination of fields, and how are duplicates identified?
reviews.fix_instructions: AC1 should specify what 'aggregated' means (e.g., total calls, unique users, etc., per time period). AC2 should define what constitutes a 'unique usage event' (e.g., based on a specific event ID or a combination of fields).

issues: The story has a strong dependency on usage calculation stories (S-003, S-004) and aggregated usage data (S-002) to ensure 'correct usage charges'.
The scope of 'generating an invoice' might be too broad, potentially encompassing the logic of other stories or significant new integration work with Stripe.
reviews.fix_instructions: Clarify the dependencies on usage calculation stories. Consider if 'generating an invoice' should be broken down further if it involves complex data assembly beyond just calling a calculation service.

issues: The story has a strong dependency on S-008 (failed payment retries completing) as dunning typically starts after payment retries are exhausted.
reviews.fix_instructions: Clarify the dependency on the failed payment retry story (S-008) and ensure it's understood that dunning starts *after* retries are exhausted.

issues: The story is too large. Retaining data for seven years and making it queryable for audit purposes involves significant architectural and implementation work, including storage solutions, data lifecycle management, and potentially a dedicated audit interface.

The acceptance criteria 'queryable and retrievable' and 'displays the requested invoice data' imply a user interface or API for accessing this data, which is a substantial piece of work not fully captured by the 'i_want' statement.
reviews.fix_instructions: Break this story down into smaller, more manageable pieces. For example, one story for establishing the long-term storage mechanism, another for ensuring data is moved to it, and another for building the audit query interface. Clarify the scope of 'queryable and retrievable' – does it include building a UI or just an API?

gaps.description: There are no explicit security requirements for the billing platform, despite handling sensitive customer usage and financial transaction data.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the security requirements for the billing platform, especially regarding data encryption, access controls, and compliance with financial data handling standards?

gaps.description: The requirements do not specify any general availability or uptime targets for the billing system, which is critical for continuous invoice generation and customer usage visibility.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the expected availability and uptime targets for the billing system, and what is the plan for disaster recovery?

gaps.description: Requirement R-002 states the system shall scale 'beyond 400 customers,' but a specific target for future scalability is not defined.
gaps.suggested_question: What is the specific target for customer scalability beyond 400? For example, are we aiming for 1,000, 5,000, or 10,000 customers within the next 1-3 years?

gaps.description: Requirement R-014 to 'automate dunning logic' lacks specific details on the dunning process, such as the number of attempts, communication channels, and timing, beyond the failed card retries.
gaps.suggested_question: Can we define the specific steps and rules for the automated dunning process, including communication content, timing, and escalation paths?

gaps.description: There is no explicit stakeholder representing the Finance or Accounting department, despite the project's direct impact on revenue recognition, tax, and audit processes.
related_ids: Goal: Accurately calculate tiered charges to ensure correct revenue recognition.
Goal: Retain seven years of invoice and usage data for tax and audit purposes.
gaps.suggested_question: Who from the Finance or Accounting department should be involved as a key stakeholder to ensure the system meets their needs for revenue recognition, reporting, and audit compliance?

gaps.coverage_note: The backlog provides good coverage for the core functional requirements of usage-based billing, including metering, tiered calculations, customer visibility, and payment processing. Most business goals are addressed by the defined requirements and stories. However, critical non-functional areas such as comprehensive security and overall system availability are not explicitly covered. There's also a need for more precise definitions for scalability targets and dunning logic. Finally, the absence of a dedicated Finance stakeholder is a notable omission for a project with significant financial implications.
